detection_definition.baseline: At least one finding from the count-based reimplementation.
detection_definition.provecode: At least one S1-S5/B1-B4 finding with severity warning or blocking.

F1.statement: On count-preserving held-out cases, PROVECODE recall exceeds the count-based baseline's.

F2.statement: On non-count-preserving cases (deletions, removed asserts), parity is expected; the baseline outperforming PROVECODE is reported.

F3.statement: Share of legitimate held-out changes flagged as blocking (wide interval at this n; Tier C is the stronger evidence).

headline: held_out
label: Injected cases on real repositories (experimental). Not real-world performance.

changes: line splitting matches the tokenizer (form feeds no longer misalign lines)
AST depth limit and RecursionError become input_limit gaps instead of crashes
S4 flags removed parametrize cases even when others are added
B2 covers class-level skips, `from pytest import mark`, and pytest.xfail(); ignores non-pytest .skip()
S1 handles positional approx tolerances and non-numeric approx; S3 flags match= loosened to match-anything
UTF-8 BOM files are analyzed; renamed test files keep their contract links

changes: case files are read as raw git objects instead of a Windows working tree where core.autocrlf had converted LF to CRLF; cases.lock.json byte hashes were regenerated

changes: TestCase subclasses are test classes; self.assert* calls are checks mapped onto S1/S2/B3
self.assertRaises*/assertWarns* feed S3; the Regex argument counts as match=
unittest.skip/skipIf/skipUnless/expectedFailure and a leading self.skipTest() are B2
tests.py and modules under tests/ are test files; renames to uncollected names are B1
revision_log.effect_on_tier_a: none: all 168 case results and all metrics identical before and after

changes: S5: a check replaced by a self-comparison or given an `or <true constant>`

revision_log.effect_on_tier_a: 17 case results changed, all of them W17-W19 weakenings, which these rules target and whose results had been seen; W17 5/6, W18 6/6, W19 6/6 now flagged; held-out recall 37 -> 43 of 44; no legitimate case changed. Recall on W17-W19 is therefore no longer an unbiased estimate; Tier A-b is the fresh evaluation of these rules
revision_log.source: ADR 0011 (rules S5 and B4), developed on the Tier A-b tuning split, not on Tier A

changes: S5 self-comparison fires only when the base check compared against a different expected value (assertTrue(r) -> assertEqual(r, r) is not a weakening)
B4 matches swallowed checks by what they check, not their text, and fires only when more checks are swallowed than before (a reworded message inside an existing try/except is not a finding)

tuning_log.change: A top-level return / pytest.skip() / `if False:` counts as a guard whenever statements follow it (or sit inside it), not only when visible asserts follow; many tests check via helpers.
